anti_overlap: fd-insurance-risk-scoring: that agent focuses on auditability and provenance of individual formula parameters; this agent focuses on the calibration workflow and comparative scoring across formula instances
fd-synth-signal-chain: that agent focuses on the Protocol contract boundary; this agent focuses on the ergonomics of iterating and comparing multiple concrete implementations of that contract

fd-pid-tuner-hotswap: that agent focuses on runtime substitution without restart; this agent focuses on offline calibration and parameter sensitivity before a formula version is promoted to production
decision_lens: Does the FeltMinutesV0 architecture support the calibration workflow that Phase 1.7 will need — iterating sun_coefficient values against OD-pair ground truth, comparing route scores, and auditing which parameter version produced a given route recommendation?
distance_rationale: Portfolio risk managers assign per-asset weight functions, run sensitivity analysis (Greeks, factor decomposition) to quantify how much each parameter contributes to the aggregate score, and A/B-compare model versions against historical outcomes — the same calibration workflow as tuning sun_coefficient against real DTLA OD pairs in Phase 1.7.
expected_isomorphisms: The risk model 'factor loading' maps to sun_coefficient: both are scalars applied to a normalized exposure measure, are expected to be empirically calibrated against realized outcomes, and are candidates for sensitivity analysis (how much does the aggregate routing score change per unit change in the factor?). The 'model comparison on the same portfolio' maps to the apply_weight A/B design: two weight instances on the same graph.
focus: Parameter sensitivity ergonomics, A/B comparison mechanics, and the calibration path from provisional default to empirically grounded coefficient
name: fd-portfolio-risk-sensitivity
persona: Apply the perspective of a quantitative risk analyst who builds factor-risk models, runs sensitivity analysis across parameter choices, and maintains a rigorous calibration workflow that distinguishes a model's in-sample fit from its out-of-sample predictive validity.
review_areas: The brainstorm identifies sun_coefficient=0.5 as provisional (synthesis finding 65) and defers calibration to Phase 1.7, but provides no calibration affordance in the Phase 1.6 design. Portfolio risk practice: the model should ship with a calibration harness (or at minimum, a parameter range and sensitivity formula) alongside the default, not just a TODO comment. The dataclass supports FeltMinutesV0(sun_coefficient=x) but there is no utility for sweeping x and scoring the result.

The open question of whether apply_weight writes two weight functions as attr='felt_minutes_a' and attr='felt_minutes_b' is treated as optional A/B support. Portfolio risk practice: model comparison is a first-class workflow, not a power-user feature. The apply_weight signature should have a more explicit pattern — e.g., apply_weights(graph, weights: Sequence[tuple[str, EdgeWeight]]) — so that multi-model comparison is the canonical path.

The frozen dataclass with replace() supports parameter tuning, but the brainstorm does not specify how to compare two FeltMinutesV0 instances' aggregate effect on the graph. Portfolio practice: a sensitivity report shows dFelt/dCoefficient per edge class (ok, partial_coverage, degenerate_short). Without this, Phase 1.7 calibration is a manual visual inspection of route changes rather than a quantified parameter sweep.

The 'neutral' fallback policy applies a fixed 0.5 sun fraction for NaN edges. Portfolio risk parallel: treating unknown exposures as neutral (mean factor loading) is a common but analytically weak choice — it hides the sensitivity contribution of NaN edges from any parameter sweep. If 30% of DTLA edges are 'no_coverage', the effective sun_coefficient is attenuated by 30% regardless of what value is filed, which should be documented as a model caveat.

There is no mechanism to score two routes against each other using the same graph with two weight functions applied. Portfolio risk practice produces a 'tracking error' between model A and model B on the same underlying assets. The brainstorm should specify whether Phase 1.7 will expose a score_route(path, weight) utility so that calibration can compare sun_coefficient=0.5 vs 0.8 on a set of reference OD pairs.

The dataclass is frozen (immutable), which is correct for value semantics. But the calibration workflow implied by Phase 1.7 — 'tune sun_coefficient against real OD pairs' — requires generating many FeltMinutesV0 instances with different coefficients. Portfolio risk tooling provides a parameter_grid() factory or a from_calibration(data) constructor; v0 expects the caller to write that loop manually.

severity_examples.condition: Phase 1.7 will calibrate sun_coefficient against 'actual DTLA OD distribution' (synthesis finding 65). Without a utility that takes a path (sequence of edges) and a weight instance and returns a scalar route score, calibration requires re-running full A* for each candidate coefficient and comparing output routes visually. This is an engineering gap that will slow Phase 1.7 and produce a weaker calibration than a parameter sweep with a quantified objective function.
severity_examples.scenario: No score_route utility means Phase 1.7 calibration has no quantitative feedback loop

severity_examples.condition: If 30% of DTLA edges have shade_data_quality='no_coverage' and receive neutral fallback (sun_fraction=0.5), the effective sun_coefficient in the aggregate routing cost is 0.5 × 0.7 + 0.5 × 0.3 × 0.5 = 0.425. This means the filed coefficient=0.5 does not equal its routing impact. A calibration that sets coefficient=0.8 to get a stronger shade preference is actually getting 0.8 × 0.7 + 0.5 × 0.3 × fallback — the model documentation should quantify this attenuation.
severity_examples.scenario: NaN-edge attenuation of sun_coefficient is undocumented as a model property

severity_examples.condition: The current interface requires apply_weight(graph, weight_a, attr='felt_minutes_a') and apply_weight(graph, weight_b, attr='felt_minutes_b') as separate calls with caller-managed naming. Portfolio practice would provide a compare_weights(graph, weights: dict[str, EdgeWeight]) -> dict[str, float] utility that runs all variants and returns aggregate statistics (mean, percentile distribution) per weight label in one call.
severity_examples.scenario: apply_weight A/B design requires manual attr= naming conventions

source_domain: Financial portfolio risk modeling and factor sensitivity analysis
success_hints: Add a score_route(path_edges: Iterable[dict], weight: EdgeWeight) -> float utility so Phase 1.7 calibration can quantify the cost difference between weight instances without re-running full A*
Document in the FeltMinutesV0 docstring the effective attenuation formula when NaN edges are present so calibration targets account for neutral-policy edges
Consider a compare_weights(graph, weights: dict[str, EdgeWeight]) helper that applies all variants and returns per-weight summary statistics as a DataFrame-ready dict
